The cfo.ai model is building now through the `cfoai` MCP, in a headless Claude run. The first attempt failed on Claude's own sign-in, and the rerun uses the project token. I report the workspace, the page and the real figures when it finishes.

content.content:
The FirstRun model is built in cfo.ai. All values below were read back from cfo.ai after the last change. One result needs your attention: under Old cap, cash goes negative in Dec 2027 (month 14).

```
WORKSPACE: Atharva CFOAI (id 102904). It is the only workspace, and its name does not mention FirstRun.
PAGE_URL: https://app.cfo.ai/s/REDACTED  (page "FirstRun model", private)
BASE: month 18 (Apr 2028) MRR $2,069, ending cash $16,832, runway: no burn (net cash flow +$1,658/month, so runway is blank)
GROWTH: month 18 MRR $5,427, ending cash $45,220, runway: no burn (net cash flow +$4,327/month)
GROSS_MARGIN: Team 85.1%, Scale 78.3% (Base, Stripe fees included in cost of revenue)
SCENARIOS:
  Tail month: Scale gross margin 44.1% vs 78.3% (Team 64.2% vs 85.1%). Ending cash $12,767 vs $16,832.
  Old cap: Scale gross margin -406.6% vs 78.3%. Ending cash -$12,131 vs $16,832. Cash first goes negative in Dec 2027 (month 14). Runway at month 18 is 0.
  Scale at $529: Scale MRR $1,855 vs $1,048. Ending cash $21,293 vs $16,832. Scale gross margin 86.5%.
  Scale at 1,500 runs: Scale gross margin 87.7% vs 78.3%. Ending cash $17,390 vs $16,832.
ASSUMPTIONS:
  - Every measured=no row in drivers.csv: vm_price_per_hour, compute_per_run, margin_floor, prices, runs per month, caps.
  - From inputs.json: Stripe 2.9% + $0.30 per paid invoice, $25 fixed costs a month, $0 founder salary, $5,000 cash on 2026-11-01, churn (Free 10%, Team 5%, Scale 3%), Base and Growth customer additions.
  - Scenario inputs from the task and BUSINESS_PLAN.md, not from drivers.csv: $0.50 old cap, $529 Scale price, 1,500 Scale runs.
  - Cost per run = cost_per_run_mean + compute_per_run ($0.01862). Old cap uses $0.50 + compute ($0.5019).
  - Cost of revenue = run cost + Stripe fees.
  - Customer counts are expected values with decimals.
PROBLEMS:
  - Variables have no description field. Each trace ID is in the "Driver source" column of the "FirstRun drivers" table, and every formula reads its number from that table.
  - cfo.ai creates a Scenario only from Main. Main holds the Base inputs. The "Base" Scenario has no changes of its own, and each of the other five changes one input on top of Main. The four test Scenarios are Base plus one change, but they are not children of the "Base" Scenario.
  - Runway is blank when net cash flow is positive. Base, Growth, Tail month and both Scale fixes have no runway number at month 18.
  - Gross margin includes Stripe fees, so Team 85.1% is lower than the 88.6% in BUSINESS_PLAN.md, which counts run cost only.
  - The page shows the Scenario comparison as a table. I did not build a Canvas chart.
  - I did not touch the existing "New Page" or its "Untitled table block". I did not create a share link or change any workspace setting.
```

**What is on the page:** a notes block first, then the month-18 Scenario comparison, the 18-month model, the plan assumptions and the drivers table.

Check: Base customer counts match the BUSINESS_PLAN.md table (month 6: Free 46.9, Team 4.5). Growth matches at month 18 (Free 255.0, Team 36.2, Scale 12.2).

The `<!-- FILL:cfo_share_link -->` line in BUSINESS_PLAN.md needs a share link. I did not make one, because your rules say not to share any page externally.

lines: -FirstRun runs a dev tool's quickstart in a clean container every night, finds the first step that breaks, proves the fix with a second clean run, and drafts the docs PR. The buyer is a DevRel or docs team at a dev-tool company.

-The business plan sets the agent's spending limit. `firstrun econ` reads every neatlogs trace, cfo.ai turns the costs into a per-tier cap, and `firstrun run --tier` stops any run that spends past it.
-## Three Tiers Price by Quickstarts Covered
-| Tier | Price per month | Quickstarts | Runs per month |
-| Scale | $299 | 100, nightly, with PRs, Docs Bisect and Prerequisite Proof | 3,000 |
-## The Average Run Costs $0.0167, but One in Twenty Costs Three Times That

-neatlogs holds 64 `firstrun.run` traces from 2026-10-10. `firstrun econ` reads them and writes [`drivers.csv`](drivers.csv), the file cfo.ai imports. Each quantile row names the trace it came from, so a judge can open the trace behind any cost in the model.
-| Driver | Cost per run | neatlogs trace |
-| Compute | $0.0019 | assumption: AWS t3.medium at $0.0416 an hour for the measured 164.8 s mean |
-The costs are Sonnet 5.5 list price, and Anthropic did not bill them. The 64 traces include 28 development runs, so the spread is wider than a production month would show.

-The expensive runs are the useful ones. A run that hits a broken step pays for recovery and for the second clean run. Of 19 real-world runs, 10 ended `verified` with 32 proven patches, and the 19 runs cost $0.97 in total. That is $0.0975 per verified quickstart (source: `runs/*/state.json`).
-## The Old $0.50 Cap Let a Scale Customer Cost Five Times the Price
-Before this plan, every run had the same cap of $0.50 in `src/firstrun/models.py`. That cap was 30 times the mean run cost, and nothing in the business set it.
-| Tier | Revenue per run | Margin at mean cost | Margin at p95 cost | Margin if every run hits $0.50 |

-The mean says both tiers are healthy. The p95 says Scale falls below a 70% margin in a month with many broken quickstarts. The old cap says one bad month can cost a Scale customer's fee five times over.
-## The Margin Floor Sets the Cap, and the Agent Enforces It
-The founder picks one number, a 70% gross margin floor. The cap for each tier is the model spend one run may use and still keep that floor:
-cap per run = price / runs per month x (1 - margin floor) - compute per run
-If every run in a month hits the cap, the tier still earns 70%. A Free run has no revenue, so its cap is the measured median run.
-| Tier | Cap per run | Measured runs over the cap |

-`firstrun run <url> --tier scale` loads the cap from [`unit_economics.json`](unit_economics.json). The executor and the recovery agent both check it, and each check is a `budget` GUARDRAIL span in neatlogs. A run that passes the cap stops with `cost budget spent`, and the report names the step where it stopped.
-On the typer quickstart, `--tier scale` verified 7/7 steps at $0.0201. `--tier free` stopped at step 4 with `cost budget spent: $0.0115 of $0.0108`.
-The cap checks FirstRun's own cost count, which runs 39% above neatlogs on 43 matched runs ($1.5253 against $1.0989). So the cap stops a run early, never late.
-## Scale Needs a Fix, and the Data Names Two
-A 25% stop rate means Scale customers would see one run in four end early. The price or the allowance has to move. Both fixes come from the same formula.
-| Option | Price | Runs per month | Cap per run | Measured runs over the cap |
-Team at $49 already stops only 7.8% of runs. A $53 price would cover the p95 run at the floor.
-## The Planner Fix From the Traces Cut Cost per Run by 24%
-neatlogs Detections and an Investigate run found the planner inventing steps. The fix shipped in commit 3ca6f11. The same 4 targets, before and after, as neatlogs measured them:
-| Agent | Model cost per run | Quickstarts finished | Failed steps recovered |
-## cfo.ai Shows the Old Cap Runs Out of Cash in Month 14

-Ari built the model in cfo.ai over MCP, in workspace "Atharva CFOAI", page "FirstRun model". Every formula reads its number from a "FirstRun drivers" table, and its "Driver source" column names the neatlogs trace behind each measured cost. The figures below were read back from cfo.ai, not computed by hand. Cost per run is $0.01862, the 64-trace mean plus compute. Gross margin includes Stripe fees.
-| Scenario | Scale gross margin | Team gross margin | Month 18 MRR | Month 18 cash |
-| Tail month: every run at p95 cost | 44.1% | 64.2% | $2,069 | $12,767 |

-Under the old cap, cash first goes negative in December 2027, month 14. Every other Scenario has positive net cash flow, so cfo.ai shows no runway limit. Raising Scale to $529 earns the most cash. Halving the Scale allowance keeps the $299 price and still clears the 70% floor.
-## Both Scenarios Pay Back Fixed Costs in Month 2
-This hand-built table came before the cfo.ai model and uses the v1 cost of $0.02771 per run. The cfo.ai table above uses the 64-trace cost, so its month 18 cash is higher.
-Both scenarios start with $5,000 cash on 2026-11-01. Fixed costs are $25 a month. Monthly churn is 10% on Free, 5% on Team and 3% on Scale. Stripe takes 2.9% plus $0.30 per paid invoice.
-- **Base:** 10 new Free users a month. 1 new Team customer a month in months 2 to 6, then 2 a month. 1 new Scale customer in months 9, 12, 15 and 18.
-- **Growth:** 30 new Free users a month. 3 new Team customers a month. 1 new Scale customer a month from month 4.
-| Scenario | Month | Free | Team | Scale | MRR | Costs | Cumulative cash |

-Customer counts are expected values, so they carry decimals. No salary is paid. With zero paying customers, $5,000 lasts about 190 months. One Team customer covers the $25 fixed costs. No customer has paid yet, so every customer count above is an assumption.
-## Rebuild the Model From the Traces
-1. Run `firstrun econ`. It reads neatlogs and rewrites `drivers.csv` and `unit_economics.json`.
-2. Attach `drivers.csv` and `inputs.json` to Ari in cfo.ai, and paste the prompt below.
-3. Run `firstrun run <url> --tier <name>`. The agent now spends inside the cap the plan set.

-FirstRun is an AI agent that runs a dev tool's quickstart docs in a clean container every night and drafts a docs pull request when a step breaks. Customers are DevRel and docs teams at developer tool companies.

-Use the attached drivers.csv for every cost. Rows with measured=yes come from neatlogs traces, and the source column names the trace. Keep that source on each Variable. Rows with measured=no are assumptions, so label them as assumptions.

-Plans: Free at $0 (4 runs a month), Team at $49 (300 runs a month), Scale at $299 (3,000 runs a month). Cost per run is cost_per_run_mean plus compute_per_run. Add Stripe at 2.9% plus $0.30 per paid invoice, $25 fixed costs a month and no founder salary. Start with $5,000 cash on 2026-11-01 and model 18 months. Use the customer additions and churn rates in inputs.json for a Base and a Growth Scenario.
-Then make four more Scenarios from Base and compare them with Base on gross margin per plan, ending cash and runway:
-1. "Tail month": cost per run is cost_per_run_p95 for every run.
-2. "Old cap": cost per run is $0.50 for every Scale run, the cap before this plan.
-4. "Scale at 1,500 runs": Scale price $299, Scale runs 1,500.
-Show customers per plan, MRR, gross margin per plan, operating costs, ending cash and cash runway.

lines: -FirstRun runs a dev tool's quickstart in a clean container every night, finds the first step that breaks, proves the fix with a second clean run, and drafts the docs PR. The buyer is a DevRel or docs team at a dev-tool company.

-The business plan sets the agent's spending limit. `firstrun econ` reads every neatlogs trace, cfo.ai turns the costs into a per-tier cap, and `firstrun run --tier` stops any run that spends past it.
-## Three Tiers Price by Quickstarts Covered
-| Tier | Price per month | Quickstarts | Runs per month |
-| Scale | $299 | 100, nightly, with PRs, Docs Bisect and Prerequisite Proof | 3,000 |
-## The Average Run Costs $0.0167, but One in Twenty Costs Three Times That

-neatlogs holds 64 `firstrun.run` traces from 2026-10-10. `firstrun econ` reads them and writes [`drivers.csv`](drivers.csv), the file cfo.ai imports. Each quantile row names the trace it came from, so a judge can open the trace behind any cost in the model.
-| Driver | Cost per run | neatlogs trace |
-| Compute | $0.0019 | assumption: AWS t3.medium at $0.0416 an hour for the measured 164.8 s mean |
-The costs are Sonnet 5.5 list price, and Anthropic did not bill them. The 64 traces include 28 development runs, so the spread is wider than a production month would show.

-The expensive runs are the useful ones. A run that hits a broken step pays for recovery and for the second clean run. Of 19 real-world runs, 10 ended `verified` with 32 proven patches, and the 19 runs cost $0.97 in total. That is $0.0975 per verified quickstart (source: `runs/*/state.json`).
-## The Old $0.50 Cap Let a Scale Customer Cost Five Times the Price
-Before this plan, every run had the same cap of $0.50 in `src/firstrun/models.py`. That cap was 30 times the mean run cost, and nothing in the business set it.
-| Tier | Revenue per run | Margin at mean cost | Margin at p95 cost | Margin if every run hits $0.50 |

-The mean says both tiers are healthy. The p95 says Scale falls below a 70% margin in a month with many broken quickstarts. The old cap says one bad month can cost a Scale customer's fee five times over.
-## The Margin Floor Sets the Cap, and the Agent Enforces It
-The founder picks one number, a 70% gross margin floor. The cap for each tier is the model spend one run may use and still keep that floor:
-cap per run = price / runs per month x (1 - margin floor) - compute per run
-If every run in a month hits the cap, the tier still earns 70%. A Free run has no revenue, so its cap is the measured median run.
-| Tier | Cap per run | Measured runs over the cap |

-`firstrun run <url> --tier scale` loads the cap from [`unit_economics.json`](unit_economics.json). The executor and the recovery agent both check it, and each check is a `budget` GUARDRAIL span in neatlogs. A run that passes the cap stops with `cost budget spent`, and the report names the step where it stopped.
-On the typer quickstart, `--tier scale` verified 7/7 steps at $0.0201. `--tier free` stopped at step 4 with `cost budget spent: $0.0115 of $0.0108`.
-The cap checks FirstRun's own cost count, which runs 39% above neatlogs on 43 matched runs ($1.5253 against $1.0989). So the cap stops a run early, never late.
-## Scale Needs a Fix, and the Data Names Two
-A 25% stop rate means Scale customers would see one run in four end early. The price or the allowance has to move. Both fixes come from the same formula.
-| Option | Price | Runs per month | Cap per run | Measured runs over the cap |
-Team at $49 already stops only 7.8% of runs. A $53 price would cover the p95 run at the floor.
-## The Planner Fix From the Traces Cut Cost per Run by 24%
-neatlogs Detections and an Investigate run found the planner inventing steps. The fix shipped in commit 3ca6f11. The same 4 targets, before and after, as neatlogs measured them:
-| Agent | Model cost per run | Quickstarts finished | Failed steps recovered |
-## cfo.ai Shows the Old Cap Runs Out of Cash in Month 14

-Ari built the model in cfo.ai over MCP, in workspace "Atharva CFOAI", page "FirstRun model". Every formula reads its number from a "FirstRun drivers" table, and its "Driver source" column names the neatlogs trace behind each measured cost. The figures below were read back from cfo.ai, not computed by hand. Cost per run is $0.01862, the 64-trace mean plus compute. Gross margin includes Stripe fees.
-| Scenario | Scale gross margin | Team gross margin | Month 18 MRR | Month 18 cash |
-| Tail month: every run at p95 cost | 44.1% | 64.2% | $2,069 | $12,767 |
-| Scale at $529 | 86.5% | 85.1% | $2,876 (Base plus the $807 Scale gain cfo.ai reported) | $21,293 |

-Under the old cap, cash first goes negative in December 2027, month 14. Every other Scenario has positive net cash flow, so cfo.ai shows no runway limit. Raising Scale to $529 earns the most cash. Halving the Scale allowance keeps the $299 price and still clears the 70% floor.
-## Both Scenarios Pay Back Fixed Costs in Month 2
-This hand-built table came before the cfo.ai model and uses the v1 cost of $0.02771 per run. The cfo.ai table above uses the 64-trace cost, so its month 18 cash is higher.
-Both scenarios start with $5,000 cash on 2026-11-01. Fixed costs are $25 a month. Monthly churn is 10% on Free, 5% on Team and 3% on Scale. Stripe takes 2.9% plus $0.30 per paid invoice.
-- **Base:** 10 new Free users a month. 1 new Team customer a month in months 2 to 6, then 2 a month. 1 new Scale customer in months 9, 12, 15 and 18.
-- **Growth:** 30 new Free users a month. 3 new Team customers a month. 1 new Scale customer a month from month 4.
-| Scenario | Month | Free | Team | Scale | MRR | Costs | Cumulative cash |

-Customer counts are expected values, so they carry decimals. No salary is paid. With zero paying customers, $5,000 lasts about 190 months. One Team customer covers the $25 fixed costs. No customer has paid yet, so every customer count above is an assumption.
-## Rebuild the Model From the Traces
-1. Run `firstrun econ`. It reads neatlogs and rewrites `drivers.csv` and `unit_economics.json`.
-2. Attach `drivers.csv` and `inputs.json` to Ari in cfo.ai, and paste the prompt below.
-3. Run `firstrun run <url> --tier <name>`. The agent now spends inside the cap the plan set.

Use the customer additions and churn rates in inputs.json for a Base and a Growth Scenario.
-Then make four more Scenarios from Base and compare them with Base on gross margin per plan, ending cash and runway:
-1. "Tail month": cost per run is cost_per_run_p95 for every run.
-2. "Old cap": cost per run is $0.50 for every Scale run, the cap before this plan.

The cfo.ai link is now in the plan, the README and the submission checklist, in PR [HighnessAtharva/firstrun#18](https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/pull/18). It is not merged yet.

- **Alerts:** I created no new ones. The 3 from earlier are listed and enabled (`56b3b8be`, `74e5d64c`, `acd01964`), so a second set would have duplicated them.
- **cfo.ai link:** I checked it signed out. https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE returns 200 with the title "How to read the FirstRun model".
- **PR #18 changes:**
  - `BUSINESS_PLAN.md` gets the link and loses the empty spreadsheet line.
  - The README cfo.ai section links the model and states that the old cap runs out of cash in month 14.
  - The cfo.ai item in the `hackathon.md` checklist is ticked.

Three items remain on the submission checklist:
1. Merge #18.

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

I built the cfo.ai story into the landing page: PR [HighnessAtharva/firstrun#19](https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/pull/19), ready to merge. It adds a section called "Plan" in the nav.

## The Story: the Business Plan Found a Bug in the Agent

Most teams will show an AI CFO's chart. Here the plan changed the agent's code, and that is the hook. The section tells it in four stops, each with a proof link:

1. **neatlogs measured** 64 runs: mean $0.0167, and one run in twenty costs $0.0508. Links to `drivers.csv`.
2. **cfo.ai modeled** 18 months from those traces. Links to your public model.
3. **The plan found** that cash runs out in month 14 under the old $0.50 cap. Links to the business plan.
4. **FirstRun fixed it:** `--tier scale` caps a run at $0.028, and a live run stopped at its cap. Links to PR #15.

**The chart** shows cash on hand for Base, Old cap and Scale at $529, using the monthly figures read back from cfo.ai. The orange line drops below zero at "Dec 2027: cash runs out". It has a hover readout and a numbers table, and two cards show the Scale fixes: $529, or 1,500 runs at $299.

**Checked:** desktop and phone, with no overlapping labels, no sideways scroll and no console errors. The palette passes the colorblind checks.

## Use the Same Story Everywhere

- **Video:** spend 20 seconds on this section. The orange line crossing zero is the cfo.ai clip.
- **X post:** "My AI CFO found a bug in my agent." Put the chart in the post.
- **Judges:** the rules ask what cfo.ai did. The answer is that it changed a line of code, and PR #15 is the proof.
